findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate scripts/gen_cli_reference.py (its curated INTERCEPT_COMMANDS dict) as an edit target, since the generator's parity self-check raises ValueError unless the new 'bridge' intercept arm has a matching curated one-liner.
evidence: gen_cli_reference.py render() self-check: 'if curated != ladder: raise ValueError(... Update INTERCEPT_COMMANDS in scripts/gen_cli_reference.py.)' (lines 148-157)
ladder_intercepts() parses `argv[0] == "<name>"` arms from _cli/__init__.py source (line 138), so a 'bridge' intercept arm is detected automatically and forces a matching curated entry
search of scripts/gen_cli_reference.py for '"bridge"' returns (no matches) — no bridge entry exists today
The plan's discovery contract (unknown nested verb 'never falls through to a same-named top-level command') implies an intercept before the dispatcher, like the audit arm
findings.finding: The plan will register 'bridge' as a new CLI arm but does not enumerate scripts/gen_cli_reference.py as an edit target, even though its curated INTERCEPT_COMMANDS dict must gain a 'bridge' entry or the generator raises ValueError — making the plan's 'Regenerate the CLI reference' step impossible without that edit.
findings.location: Approach: 'Regenerate the CLI reference and document only the staged surface'
scenarios: Author runs `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` after adding the bridge intercept and it aborts with the INTERCEPT_COMMANDS drift ValueError
findings.suggested_fix: Add scripts/gen_cli_reference.py to the edit set: add a curated INTERCEPT_COMMANDS['bridge'] one-liner describing the noun so render()'s ladder-vs-curated parity check passes, then regenerate docs/cli-reference.md.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add docs/exit-codes.md to the docs edit set with a `bridge` (and per-verb, as needed) exit/stream row, since test_exit_codes_doc_conformance derives arms from _INTERCEPTS | known_subcommands() and fails for any undocumented arm.
evidence: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes_doc_conformance.py dispatcher_arms() = set(cli._INTERCEPTS) | set(_help.known_subcommands()) (line 28), asserted against `| \`<name>\`` rows in docs/exit-codes.md
search of docs/exit-codes.md for '| `bridge' returns only bridge-fsck (line 93) and bridge-probe (line 132) — no 'bridge' noun row
The plan pins 'exit/stream contracts' for bridge but does not list docs/exit-codes.md among the docs it updates
findings.finding: Adding 'bridge' as a dispatcher arm forces a new row in docs/exit-codes.md (the mechanical conformance oracle unions _INTERCEPTS | known_subcommands()), but the plan's docs list names only cli-reference.md, user-guide.md, and release-notes.md — omitting exit-codes.md.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'docs/cli-reference.md, docs/user-guide.md, and docs/release-notes.md describe the staged surface'
scenarios: `make test` runs test_every_dispatcher_arm_has_an_exit_code_row and reports 'bridge' has no exit-codes row
The pinned-exit-contract AC cannot be documented where the conformance oracle looks
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate docs/exit-codes.md as an edit target and add a `| \`bridge\` | ... |` row (matching how the wiring exposes the noun) so the mechanical dispatcher-arm conformance test passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Approach claim that `--max-changes`/`--only`/`--except`/`--max-age` 'remain with 4a44': these flags do not currently exist on the reconciler CLI (only --repo-root/--mode/--dry-run-enumerate/--filter-local-ids do), so state whether 4a44 must ADD them rather than merely inherit them.
evidence: Reconciler argparse defines exactly four flags: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:493 (--repo-root), :501 (--mode), :509 (--dry-run-enumerate), :519 (--filter-local-ids).
search_files for 'max-changes', '--only', '--max-age' across src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler returned (no matches).
MISMATCH: the word 'remain' presupposes an existing public surface; the verified argparse surface does not contain these flags.
Flags this plan DOES depend on are Verified: --mode (:501) forces dry-run/live; --filter-local-ids (:519) is the flag the plan rejects.
findings.finding: The Approach asserts four reconciler flags ('Public `--max-changes`, `--only`, `--except`, and `--max-age` remain with 4a44') as if they already exist on the reconciler CLI surface, but none of the four exist anywhere in the reconciler argparse; the verified surface is only --repo-root, --mode, --dry-run-enumerate, and --filter-local-ids.
scenarios: A reader/reviewer or the sibling 4a44 author treats these four as pre-existing reconciler flags and only re-homes routing, when 4a44 must actually ADD them from scratch.

evidence: 7 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.finding: The Approach asserts that '--max-changes, --only, --except, and --max-age remain with 4a44', framing them as existing public reconciler flags whose migration another story owns; but the reconciler CLI defines only --repo-root, --mode, --dry-run-enumerate, and --filter-local-ids, so none of these four flags exist on the current surface.
scenarios: A reviewer or downstream story assumes preview/sync inherit these public flags from the reconciler and only need to pass them through
Story 4a44 is scoped to 'retain' flags that were never implemented, so the flags silently never ship
